rule.description: A unified adaptor interface with at least 8 members covering multiple unrelated capability areas forces classes that realize it (directly, through base classes, or through structural member coverage) to carry members they only provide as placeholders or not at all, while another implementor provides the same members genuinely.

checks.description: A unified adaptor interface declares members spanning unrelated capability areas (raw storage, the Next.js incremental-cache entry protocol, and the tags manifest lifecycle) and forces members onto implementors that cannot use them, while at least one other implementor provides those members genuinely.
checks.detected_relation: >= 8-member interface -> forced placeholder or missing member provisions across its implementor classes
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The interface exceeds every implementor's dependency boundary, mixing capability areas that belong to different participants of the cache subsystem.

matches.evidence: SuspenseCacheAdaptor declares 12 members covering raw storage, the entry protocol and the manifest lifecycle, and forces 12 member provisions onto the storage backends (KVAdaptor, CacheApiAdaptor) while the composite implementor provides each forced member genuinely.

checks.description: A unified adaptor interface member belonging to the entry protocol or the tags manifest lifecycle is forced onto a storage backend that provides it only as a throwing placeholder, while another implementor provides it genuinely.
checks.detected_relation: interface member -> placeholder provision on a storage backend class (bound implementor or structural cover)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The backend's dependency boundary covers only raw storage; the declared conformance forces it to carry capability members it cannot use.

excluded.what: single-purpose declared interfaces in the package (for example environment-binding and service-designator style interfaces)
excluded.why: they cover one capability area and do not force members onto any implementor

excluded.what: class-inheritance relationships without a widened declared contract
excluded.why: forced-capability obligations are introduced by the unified interface, not by inheritance alone

excluded.what: type declarations, test helpers and build output directories
excluded.why: not production implementors of the analysed contract
